task_name: Ironwood Kitchen - Product launch video package
client_brief:
Ironwood Kitchen is introducing the lunch range and we want it cut short and honest. What came back from the kitchen is one five second take, which is nowhere near a film, so the completed source pack adds the missing coverage and a cleared instrumental bed before anyone starts editing. Nothing here is narrated. These play muted in a feed and on the site, so the words sit on screen and the bed does the rest.

Please build a 12 to 15 second launch film in 16:9, cut from at least five different takes, and an 8 to 10 second upright cutdown that puts a complete bowl on screen inside the first two seconds. Both carry the supplied bed, both close on the Ironwood Kitchen wordmark, and both show the price “$12” exactly as ironwood_skus.csv has it. Keep the claims to the two cleared lines in ironwood_notes.txt, the protein per bowl and the no added sugar in dressings. Anything past those two lines is not approved and we will send it back.

The rest of the package is unchanged. We still need the eight bowl product modules with the complete bowl in frame and no reference card, the two page lunch range line sheet with names bound to the SKU register, and the film cover.

brand_identity.tagline: Real lunch, in the case by half ten
brand_identity.sector: Fast casual grab and go: high protein meal prep bowls sold from a counter case and by office park delivery.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Providence, Rhode Island, two counters and three office park delivery routes run by a small kitchen crew.
brand_identity.about: Ironwood Kitchen builds honest, high protein bowls for the office lunch run, in the fridge case by mid morning and gone by early afternoon. We are a working kitchen, not a tasting room. The promise is simple: food you would actually eat at your desk, twelve dollars, nothing invented and nothing dressed up.
brand_identity.audience: Office workers 24 to 45 on a weekday lunch run with roughly eleven minutes to spend, buying on macros, speed and trust rather than on spectacle.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve dollars a bowl, the everyday middle of grab and go. Above a supermarket meal deal, well below a chef counter. We are not a tasting menu and never pretend to be one.
brand_identity.typography: Schibsted Grotesk Bold carries the package. The signature move is the level price: bowl name and price share one baseline at an identical 88 px, name in Ink Charcoal and figure in Salsa Clay, one em apart, tracked minus two percent, so a viewer notices first a price drawn as large as the food. Schibsted Grotesk Regular sets the allergen and macro line at 28 px on 38 px leading, the closing line Medium at 72 px; printed case labels set names 22 pt, body 9 pt on 12 pt. Never print the price smaller than the name.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, counter honest, one thought per line. Example: "Twelve bucks, in the case by half ten, gone by two. That is the whole promise."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand kit survives. The wordmark exists only as a flat picture on a white ground, exported by a designer who has since left, with no vector file and no source anywhere. Everything else is a photograph or a spreadsheet.
brand_identity.values: Feed people well and tell the truth about what is in the bowl. The allergen line and the macros are not marketing, they are the deal.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The bowl name and the price sit on one shared baseline at exactly the same size, name in Ink Charcoal and price in Salsa Clay one em apart, so the twelve dollars is drawn as large as the food it buys.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
